S2 T2 sportive-statued-goose IMPLEMENTED and PUSHED: Gerrit 1896, rebased onto origin/main 4d1d2d3ad9 first (RP-04 C3a-JIRA and four more commits had landed). binding_lifecycle.py 267 -> 495 LOC, binding_store.py 646 -> 539. All 11 members plus _env_int, _DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE and the RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE read moved; both config_ownership_exceptions.py rows RETARGETED to the binding_lifecycle.py path with MOVED-legacy-ambient-read rationales and the stale L538/L110 prose corrected; ADR 0099 section 9 forward note updated to REALIZED; docs/env-vars.md regenerated. check_config_ownership.py exit 0, make lint 0, typecheck 566 Success, 3302 passed + 9 skipped.
HELD-OUT: all 13 withheld discriminators passed unseen (clear_absent no-dirty, unbound no-ops, defensive env parse, retire/unretire alerts, unretire idempotency, tombstone isolation on retire and on lift, comment no-churn, legacy-store no-rewrite, corrupt-retired fail-open, alert-failure survivability, unknown-field survival on the wholesale-rewritten retired file). Implementer: 1 attempt.
MUTATION FOUND TWO TAUTOLOGIES, and they resolved differently - worth distinguishing. (a) REAL GAP: my no-churn test compared bytes before/after, which cannot fail, because record_comment_id stamps no timestamp so an unconditional save re-serializes byte-IDENTICAL content. Replaced with a WRITE-COUNTING oracle that patches the repository save and asserts zero writes on an identical re-record and exactly one on a new mapping; re-verified RED under the mutation. (b) NOT A GAP: _env_int's minimum clamp is behaviorally UNOBSERVABLE through note_absent, because the counter is incremented before the comparison, so grace 0 or -3 retires on the first 404 exactly as a clamped 1 does. I did NOT manufacture a test for an unobservable difference (that would assert internal structure); the parametrized case pins the observable outcome and the commit records why.
THIRD FALSE DOCUMENTED CLAIM FOUND IN THIS EPIC. My new test test_a_key_is_never_remapped_to_a_different_id FAILED, and the code was right: the comment-map change-gate is equality-only, so a DIFFERING id overwrites and saves. Verified against the pre-extraction source at 4758d47f82 - identical logic - so the extraction is faithful and the docstring's 'a key is never remapped to a different id' was always false. Corrected the docstring where it moved into binding_lifecycle.py rather than carrying a false statement forward, and pinned the real overwrite behavior in test_a_differing_id_for_a_known_key_overwrites_and_saves. Making the map genuinely append-only would be a behavior change needing its own ticket. Pattern across this epic: safety-abort-on-double-bind (S2 plan), alert dedup via timestamp_ns (S1 T1), and now never-remapped - three documented guarantees the code never implemented.
SURFACE-PARITY CENSUS done explicitly for the new review overlay and recorded in the commit message: CLI, MCP/API and public library facade all OUT OF SCOPE and verified by grep (no _cli/ or _commands/ caller, no MCP tool, and BindingStore is not exported from rebar/__init__.py - it is an internal _engine module); automated callers IN SCOPE and proven (six reconciler modules, their suites pass unmodified); dual-direction IN SCOPE and proven on both read/write pairs with unretire as retire's tested inverse. NOTE: rebar review-code could NOT preview locally - this checkout has verify.enable_code_review off - so the census in the commit message is the mitigation and the real gate runs server-side.
RESIDUAL GAP TO FILE: the implementer flagged that tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py:311 patches binding_store_mod._now_iso to advance the clock, but clear_absent now resolves _now_iso from binding_lifecycle, so that patch no longer covers it. The test still passes and the contract IS covered directly by my held-out clear_absent no-dirty test, so coverage moved tiers rather than disappearing - but the integration oracle's blast radius narrowed and should be widened to patch both modules.
